Craspedocephalus malabaricus (Malabar pit viper), family Viperidae. WHO category in India: Category 2. Danger: dangerous (WHO Category 2; India Category 2; listed as Trimeresurus (Craspedocephalus) malabaricus). Told apart from Hypnale hypnale (Hump-nosed pit viper), Echis carinatus (Saw-scaled viper): Both sides are dangerous, but Indian polyvalent antivenom is raised against the Big Four and may not work on hump-nosed or Malabar pit vipers (WHO SEARO 2016, PDF p. 143). Hump-nosed bites in Kerala were misidentified as saw-scaled viper bites (M1 report ref 31).

Echis carinatus (Saw-scaled viper), family Viperidae. WHO category in India: Category 1. Danger: dangerous (WHO Category 1; India Category 1). Told apart from Boiga trigonata (Common cat snake): Vipers have many small rough scales covering the crown of the head (WHO SEARO 2016, PDF p. 30), and the saw-scaled viper makes a grating rasp when threatened (WHO SEARO 2016, PDF p. 70). Told apart from Hypnale hypnale (Hump-nosed pit viper), Craspedocephalus malabaricus (Malabar pit viper): Both sides are dangerous, but Indian polyvalent antivenom is raised against the Big Four and may not work on hump-nosed or Malabar pit vipers (WHO SEARO 2016, PDF p. 143). Hump-nosed bites in Kerala were misidentified as saw-scaled viper bites (M1 report ref 31).
